title: A binding price ceiling on kayak rentals: the shortage, the quantity rented and deadweight loss
scenario: In Lake Mirren, an invented resort town, the market for hourly kayak rentals is in equilibrium at $30 an hour with 200 rentals a day. The town council sets a maximum price of $20 an hour. At $20, visitors want 260 rentals a day and rental shops offer 140.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Draw a correctly labeled graph of the market for kayak rentals and show the price ceiling.

rubric.point: A correctly labeled graph: price and quantity axes, downward-sloping demand, upward-sloping supply
accept: P and Q axes with D and S labeled

rubric.point: A horizontal price ceiling line below the equilibrium price

parts.sample: Vertical axis: Price; horizontal axis: Quantity of rentals. Demand D slopes down and supply S slopes up, crossing at $30 and 200 rentals. A horizontal line labeled Pc is drawn at $20, below the crossing, with Qs (140) and Qd (260) marked where it meets S and D.

slips.Pc: A ceiling above the $30 equilibrium would not bind; the $20 ceiling sits below it.

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Calculate the size of the shortage. Show your work.

rubric.point: 120 rentals, with work: 260 demanded minus 140 supplied

parts.sample: Shortage = quantity demanded − quantity supplied at $20 = <math class="mic-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>260</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>140</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>120</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">260 - 140 = 120</annotation></semantics></math> rentals a day.

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: Identify the number of kayak rentals that take place each day under the ceiling, and explain.

rubric.point: 140 rentals, because only the quantity shops supply at $20 can be rented (the smaller of Qd and Qs)

parts.sample: 140 rentals a day. A rental needs both a visitor and a shop, and shops offer only 140 at $20, so the quantity traded is the quantity supplied.

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: Shade the deadweight loss caused by the price ceiling.

rubric.point: Shades the triangle between demand and supply from the quantity supplied at the ceiling out to the equilibrium quantity
accept: the triangle between D and S from Qs to QE

parts.sample: The deadweight loss is the triangle bounded by demand above, supply below, and the vertical line at the quantity supplied at the ceiling, running out to the equilibrium quantity where the curves cross.

slips.transfer: That rectangle is surplus moved from shops to renters, not lost.
